instructions: Finely chop 1/2 cup of the onion. Grate 2 tbsp of the carrot and 1 tsp of the ginger. Tear about 6 curry leaves and chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds. When they crackle, add the curry leaves and stir for a few seconds.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the onion turns pink. Add the ginger and cilantro and stir for 30 seconds.
Transfer the mix to a bowl and let it cool for a few minutes.
Stir the cooled mix into the batter. Add a pinch of salt only if the batter needs it. It should be medium thick, so add a spoonful of water if it's too stiff.
Heat a paniyaram pan over medium heat. Add a few drops of oil to each hollow and wipe it around.
Fill each hollow about three-quarters full with batter. Lower the heat to medium-low and cook for about 2 minutes, covered if you like, until the bottoms are golden.
Uncover, cook for 1 minute, then flip each one with a wooden skewer or spoon. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden all over and cooked through in the middle.
Transfer to a plate. Add a few drops of oil to each hollow and repeat with the rest of the batter to make 15 to 20. Serve warm with the coconut chutney.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes leads (5 stars from 59): idli or dosa batter mixed with a mustard seed, curry leaf, onion and ginger tempering, then cooked in a paniyaram pan until golden. Nish Kitchen (5 from 41) uses the same method with urad dal in the tempering and a little asafoetida, which is left out here because some brands carry wheat. The green chilies are left out to keep it mild. Check the batter label: most are rice and urad dal only, so they're gluten-free and vegan. It needs a paniyaram pan, and the batches take about 35 minutes all in.
